title: KINBERT and phospho-PCA map kinase-substrate interactions, including understudied kinases
summary: KINBERT, a protein language model encoding catalytic domains and substrate peptides, was combined with the pooled phospho-PCA screening assay and Bayesian hierarchical modeling. The framework identified novel high-confidence substrates for 23 kinase constructs representing 21 kinases, including the understudied ADCK1 and CaMKK1. Trained on literature-curated data, KINBERT outperformed existing models on standard and out-of-distribution benchmarks, and improved when phospho-PCA data were added. Only the abstract was reviewed.
ai_technology: KINBERT protein language model for kinase-substrate interaction prediction, trained with phospho-PCA data

evidence.tested: Pooled phospho-PCA experiments and applications including live-cell biosensors for TBK1 and IKKbeta.
evidence.unknown: Per-substrate validation rates and effect sizes, not given in the abstract; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: The language model learned interaction rules and, with the assay data, ranked candidate substrates.
